card.title: Nintendo Switch Short Circuit Detection and M92T36 Power Management Checks

claims.statement: Continuity on both sides of a capacitor when checked against ground indicates a short to ground.
claims.evidence: Checking capacitors with a multimeter set to continuity mode with black probe on a good ground.
claims.quote: with a multimeter set to continuity mode, put the black probe on a good ground... and with the red probe check every capacitor... continuity in both sides of the capacitor means short to ground.

claims.statement: Pin 5 of the M92T36 is an input line that should read 3V to 6V, and Pin 6 is an output line that should read between 3V and 6V when the power button is pressed.
claims.evidence: DC voltage measurement on M92T36 pins 5 and 6 or their respective trace capacitors.
claims.quote: touch the pin 5 of M92T36... In that pin you are supposed to have 3v to 6v. If you have 0v or less, you have a short on that line... touch the pin 6 or the capacitor on the end of the trace and its suppose to have betwee

claims.statement: M92T36 handles power negotiation via USB-C and video out; damage causes charging and HDMI video output failures.
claims.evidence: M92T36 failure symptoms and pin function analysis.
claims.quote: M92T36 chip is responsible for negotiating power through the USB-C port, which happens to also be the port through which HDMI out video passes through. When damaged, the negotiations fail, causing both charging problems

procedure: Unplug the battery and remove components on top of the motherboard except the eMMC chip.
Set multimeter to continuity mode, place black probe on ground (metal shield or USB-C port), and probe both sides of capacitors across the front and back of the motherboard.
Inspect M92T36 pins for shorts to ground.
Reinstall the motherboard into the frame with the battery connected, press the power button, set multimeter to DC voltage, and test M92T36 Pin 5 and Pin 6 (or their corresponding trace capacitors).
tools: Multimeter with fine probe tip or soldered paper pin
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Probing live pins with standard thick multimeter probes can easily slip and cause accidental shorts.
card.caveats: Finding a shorted capacitor near a chip does not automatically prove the chip is dead; remove the capacitor to verify if the short clears.
